source.text: *ጠይቁ፡ ወርእዩ፡ *ኵሎ፡ ዕፀወ፡ እፎ፡ ያስተርእዩ፡ ከመ፡ ይቡስ፡ ወኵሉ፡ አቊጽሊሆሙ፡ ንጉፍ፡ ዘእንበለ፡ *፲ወ፬ዕፀው፡ ዘኢይትነገፉ፡ አላ፡ ይጸንሑ፡ እምብሉይ፡ እስከ፡ ይመጽእ፡ ኃዲስ፡ እም*ክልኤ፡ ወእም፡ ፫ክረምት።
source.note: Complete selected Charles 1906 printed page 6, from III to before IV. Four editorial asterisks and baseline numerals are retained; raised apparatus calls are excluded. Separate Uoft camera and fresh pinned-PDF render show the same selected print, not distinct manuscript witnesses. The scope of the closing time expression remains uncertain; no source ending is supplied from a comparison witness.

transcription_uncertainties.issue: The connected middle-height lateral feature favors labialized Qaf II ቊ, which is retained, but the II versus V order is the least secure fine typographic distinction in this selected print. This is not a missing character or a lexically different foliage noun.
transcription_uncertainties.treatment: Retain the visually favored selected-edition spelling and low confidence; do not choose the order from English or normalize the Ethiopic. Distinct exact review must examine the selected glyph against both controls.

transcription_uncertainties.location: 1 Enoch 3:1, እም*ክልኤ፡ ወእም፡ ፫ክረምት (closing time expression)
transcription_uncertainties.issue: The printed words and the two numbers are retained. The attachment of the repeated temporal preposition remains uncertain; the printed unit ends normally and does not have a lacuna.
transcription_uncertainties.treatment: Keep “from two and from three years” and note c’s explicit qualification, with no implied exact duration, “or,” or ending from another witness.

translation.text: Examine and see all the trees, how they appear as though dry,[a] with all their foliage fallen, except for fourteen trees that do not shed their leaves.[b] But they remain from the old until the new comes—from two and from three years.[c]

footnotes.text: “As though dry” describes how the trees appear; it does not say they were not dry. Dillmann cites Enoch 3 under appearance or resemblance (column 298) and the dry participle (column 1071). The connective can also introduce what is perceived rather than a comparison. The surviving Greek text at this point supports the opening commands and “all the trees,” but breaks off before the drying clause.

Charles prints fourteen in the body; apparatus note 27 records variation in the count. Dillmann’s entry (columns 695–696) cites Enoch 3 both for the fallen or shed participle and for trees shedding their own leaves or being stripped of foliage. The translation follows the printed exception without identifying a species.

“The old” and “the new” likely refer to foliage, but the Ethiopic does not repeat a noun here. The closing words preserve two, three and both instances of “from”; it is unclear exactly how this time phrase attaches. The final noun can mean winter or rainy season, but Dillmann cites this passage under “year” (column 834). The wording does not resolve the phrase into a definite “for two or three years,” or supply a missing ending from another witness.
